items.b: SEC SUES LUGANO'S FORMER CHIEF OVER MORE THAN $1 BILLION OF FICTITIOUS REVENUE
items.t: The complaint against Mordechai Ferder was filed 31 August in the Central District of California, case 8:26-cv-02492, and released 1 September as Litigation Release 26625. Compass Diversified restated Lugano's net identifiable assets at acquisition from $179 million to $5 million and erased over 85% of the revenue it had reported since. Ferder denies the allegations.

items.b: CHOW TAI SENG'S HONG KONG SUBSIDIARY ADMITTED TO THE SHANGHAI GOLD EXCHANGE
items.t: Board announcement 2026-043, dated 2 September, says the Shenzhen-listed chain learned on 31 August that its wholly-owned Hong Kong arm is an international member of the exchange. The filing states no purpose and no financial effect. First-half revenue fell 20.79% to RMB 3.641 billion and net profit 24.24% to RMB 450 million.

items.b: PERTH MINT MINTED SALES FALL IN ALL THREE METALS AS PRICES ROSE
items.t: August sales were 23,932 ounces of gold, 333,880 of silver and 1,060 of platinum, down 22%, 31% and 45% on July. Gold ran from about $4,050 to about $4,450 in the same month. Holdings in the mint's gold-backed product went the other way, up 13,137 ounces or 3.43% to 395,871.

items.b: ROLEX SENDS FOUR ONE-OFF DAYTONAS TO PHILLIPS LONDON ON 28 SEPTEMBER
items.t: The Four Seasons set was conceived as a private sale to one buyer at about 4 million Swiss francs, roughly $4.9 million, and moved to auction after retailer feedback. Proceeds split evenly between the Federer Foundation and Re:wild. No estimate has been published and the lotting is not stated.

items.b: FOUR METALS CLOSED LOWER ON FRIDAY AND THE BOARD IS FROZEN THROUGH THE WEEKEND
items.t: Gold $4,429.10, down $43.10 or 0.9637%; silver $66.091, down $0.756; platinum $1,816.00, down $1.00; palladium $1,368.00, down $33.00 or 2.3555%. Kitco's board carries an identical 2026-09-04 17:00 timestamp on all four, which is what establishes the session as closed rather than the day of the week.

items.b: CIBJO'S VOTE ON DROPPING “LABORATORY-GROWN” IS SET FOR 7 SEPTEMBER, NOT YET TAKEN
items.t: The centenary congress runs 4 to 7 September in Vicenza. Trade reports of the Blue Book change describe a scheduled vote, and no source read this morning records it as carried. Carat Capital reported the proposal on 27 July and is holding the outcome until the assembly has actually voted.
